newsitem.title: UK: UK charity fund returns off '95 but still good - WM.
newsitem.headline: UK charity fund returns off '95 but still good - WM.

text.p: Britain's 350 charity funds, which manage assets of over 10 billion stg, performed strongly in 1996 but failed to top the "spectacular" returns of 1995, according to a report on the sector from the WM Company.

They had total returns of over 11 percent "well ahead of retail price inflation at around two percent", according to WM, a major investment performance measurement consultancy. In 1995, returns topped 19 percent.
"The 1996 performance reflected strong equity returns from the UK, North America and Continental Europe," Peter Warrington, a director of WM, said.

"Over the medium and longer terms, the picture is equally bright, with real annual returns (over and above inflation) averaging seven percent during the last 10 years and over 11 percent during the past five years."
"The UK market really delivered the goods for UK charities with returns of over 17 percent, with the average active manager outperforming the FTSE All-share Index."
North America returned 14 percent but Japan lagged with negative 23 percent.
He noted that North American returns were dragged down by the nine percent appreciation of the pound against the dollar, but the funds still managed to outperform the S&P 500 index.
Sterling also appreciated about 16 percent against European currencies and 19 percent on the yen.

Charity funds currently have a high cash weighting, having taken profits in Britain and North America. "...the funds are awaiting a downturn before returning to buy at lower levels," the report added.
Analysis of charity funds with different investment objectives has revealed little difference in performance between those with asset mix or income constraints and those with none.

"Historically, funds with constraints have had a higher weighting in UK bonds and a correspondingly lighter exposure to overseas equity markets but this did not hold them back in 1996," the report said.
